aff::integration.debugDescription: If tracking isn’t working correctly, please review the following points carefully, one by one:
aff::integration.debugNote: Note: When using the test referral link, visits, signups and customers won’t appear on the dashboard. We recommend creating an Affiliate and simulating the entire flow using their referral link (clear cookies or use incognito mode beforehand).
aff::integration.debugStep1: Make sure you visited the test link ({testLink}) in an incognito window. If you have multiple incognito windows open, it’s better to close them first since they share the same session.
aff::integration.debugStep10: If using "Option 2) Tracking on a redirected page", place the script near the one from step 1. This script initializes data to be sent when am.js loads. If it’s placed inside a function called after am.js loads or after non-async loading scripts, it won’t work. If you can’t place it in the </head> tag near the first script, put it at the beginning of the </body> tag.
aff::integration.debugStep2: Ensure that am.js is loaded on the page. The script from step 1 should also be on the same page as the script from step 2 (signup tracking). Use your browser's inspector to verify that the script is loading.
aff::integration.debugStep3: Check if the tracking cookie is set. The signup tracking function is only called when the cookie is set via a referral link. Before proceeding with a test signup or conversion, ensure the "am_id" cookie is present. If it’s not, recheck steps 1 and 2, along with step 5.
aff::integration.debugStep4: If the cookie is set, verify that there is a call to "/affiliate-manager/affiliate-campaign/v2/external-lead" when you complete the signup. If previous steps are correct, and you know the signup tracking script has been reached (you can use console.log to verify), but there’s no call to that URL, use the following steps to debug.
aff::integration.debugStep5:
Ensure the domain in the script matches the current domain you’re testing on. The visitor tracking script (from step 1) includes your original domain. If this domain differs from the current domain (not the subdomain), the cookie won’t be read.

The script works across different subdomains (e.g, website.com => app.website.com or blog.website.com => app.website.com), but NOT across different domains (e.g. website.com => anothersite.com).
aff::integration.debugStep6: It should work on your staging subdomain (staging.website.com), but for testing on localhost or similar, you’ll need to temporarily replace the domain in the first script with your localhost domain (don’t forget to change it back before pushing to production).
aff::integration.debugStep7: Ensure the email value is valid. If you pass the email parameter, make sure it has a valid format.
aff::integration.debugStep8: If you're using "Option 1) Tracking based on JS event", ensure the page doesn’t perform a full redirect immediately after affiliateManager.trackLead is called. If the page reloads, all requests are canceled. If using Javascript for redirection, use a setTimeout with at least a 1-second delay.
aff::integration.debugStep9: If your signup/order form is inside an iframe from a different domain, either redirect the /thank-you page to the main domain OR use the postMessage JS function to send a notification to the parent window when the signup is complete (along with the data) and call affiliateManager.trackLead from the parent window.
aff::integration.option1Step1Alert: This script tracks leads, while actual sales tracking is managed server-side through the Stripe webhook.
aff::integration.option1Step1Title: 1. Place the script below within the success callback function of the signup or in the form's onSubmit event (if the page doesn't redirect afterward).
aff::integration.option1Step2Alert: affiliateManager.trackLead has a callback function that gets called after the signup request is received, in case of an error or if no referral was found.
aff::integration.option1Step2Title: 2. Replace either <user-email> or <user-stripe-customer-id> with the corresponding data collected from the signup form. For example, if you're using jQuery and the email field's ID is 'email', you can substitute <user-email> with $('#email').val(). Note that the "email" is optional if you decide to use "uid" instead (details below).
aff::integration.option2Step1Alert: This script tracks leads, while actual sales tracking is managed server-side through the Stripe webhook.
aff::integration.option2Step1Title: 1. Place the script below right before the </head> tag on the page users land on after the initial conversion (trial or free plan signup) or sale (if you don’t provide a free trial). Ensure that existing users do not access this page; therefore, avoid adding the script to the dashboard. Instead, include it on a thank you or confirmation page intended for new users.
aff::integration.option2Step2Title: 2. You need to replace either "uid" or "email" with the corresponding submitted data from the server. If you use "uid," "email" is optional (see below).
aff::integration.step1Description: Add the affiliate tracking script before the </head> tag on your website
aff::integration.step2AlertContent: If you choose either option, make sure the visitor tracking script from the previous step is also included on the page where the selected script is placed. These scripts are also compatible with subdomains.
aff::integration.step2Description: You have two options to track sign-ups. Select the one that best fits your application and you're most comfortable using.
aff::integration.step2Option1Description: For single-page applications (SPA) or when the signup form is submitted through an XMLHttp request, this is the recommended approach. However, if you are using a standard signup form that redirects users upon submission, it's better to go with Option 2 (Tracking on a redirected page).
aff::integration.step2Option1Title: Option 1) Tracking based on a Javascript event
aff::integration.step2Option2Description: Select this option if you redirect users to a new page following a signup or sale. The tracking request will be initiated when the tracking script from the first step loads, which essentially prepares the data to be sent.
aff::integration.step2Option2Title: Option 2) Tracking on a redirect page
aff::integration.uidAlertDescription: The "uid" value should match the Customer ID from Stripe.
aff::integration.uidDescription1: To match the lead submitted via the signup tracking script with the customer in Stripe, our system primarily relies on the "email" field. In most cases, this works seamlessly, as the system will automatically sync the customer using their ID once the first sale is made and keep the records updated.
aff::integration.uidDescription2: However, there are situations where using only the "email" may not be ideal or feasible. For example, if you prefer not to share user email addresses with third parties (to minimize GDPR concerns) or if the signup email differs from the Stripe email at the time of the first payment. In these cases, an additional identifier, the "uid" is required.
aff::integration.uidDescription3: The "uid" is generally necessary if any of the following conditions apply:
aff::integration.uidOption1: You prefer not to share lead's or customer's email addresses with the system.
aff::integration.uidOption2: Users on free trials or freemium plans may use a different email during checkout than the one they signed up with.
aff::integration.uidOption3: Free trial or freemium users frequently change their email before completing their first payment.
aff::integration.uidTitle: Understanding the "uid" parameter and when it's necessary

Can I run {campaignName}s for leads instead of sales?
aff::onboarding.learnMore.accordion.coup: If you assign a unique coupon code to an {affiliateName}, any sale using that code will be tracked and credited to them, even without the {affiliateName} link.
What happens if someone uses a coupon instead of a {affiliateName} link?
aff::onboarding.learnMore.accordion.defa: This is the standard reward you set for each sale or lead. You can apply it across all products or customize it per product or per {affiliateName}.
aff::onboarding.learnMore.accordion.diff: Yes. You can set a custom rate per {affiliateName} within any {campaignName} to reward top performers or partners differently.
Can I assign different commission rates to different {affiliateName}s?
aff::onboarding.learnMore.accordion.howD: You set up a {campaignName} and invite {affiliateName}s to join. They share a {affiliateName} link, and when someone makes a purchase or signs up through it, the system automatically tracks the {affiliateName} and calculates the commission.
aff::onboarding.learnMore.accordion.howT: You can add {affiliateName}s manually, import them from your {contactNames} list, or let them sign up through a public registration form.

Once a sale or lead is tracked, the system logs the commission. You can review and approve it, then pay {affiliateName}s via connected gateways like PayPal or through manual methods such as bank transfer.
aff::onboarding.learnMore.accordion.mult: This allows {affiliateName}s to earn from others they refer into your program. For example, if {affiliateName} A refers {affiliateName} B, A can earn a percentage of B's referred sales.
aff::onboarding.learnMore.accordion.payo: {payoutName} delay lets you hold commissions for a period (e.g., NET 15, NET 30) before they become eligible for {payoutName} — useful for handling refunds or subscription churn.
aff::onboarding.learnMore.accordion.refe: You can manually credit a commission if a sale or lead was missed, using offline records or custom attribution.
What if a {affiliateName} doesn't track automatically?
aff::onboarding.learnMore.accordion.what: An {affiliateName} is someone who promotes your business and earns a commission for every sale or lead they refer through their unique link or code.
It's a unique URL assigned to each {affiliateName}. When clicked, it tracks who referred the visitor so the right {affiliateName} can be credited.

A cookie is a small tracking file placed on a visitor's browser when they click an {affiliateName} link. If that visitor makes a purchase within the cookie window (e.g., 30 days), the {affiliateName} gets credit.

cal-b::calendarAI.messages.workingHoursE:
Working hours are managed through **Availability Schedules**.

**What is a Schedule?**
A schedule defines the days and time slots when you (or your team) are available for bookings. For example: mon–fri, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM.

**Who can set availability?**
- **You** — set your own schedule from the availability settings.
- **Team members** — each team member can have their own schedule, so bookings only happen when they're free.
- **Per calendar** — you can assign different schedules to different calendars (e.g. "Morning consultations" vs "Afternoon classes").

**Multiple schedules**
You can create as many schedules as you need — for example, "Weekday hours", "Weekend hours", or "Holiday hours" — and assign them to the right calendars.

To manage your schedules, open the availability settings below.

isv::emailServices.smtpServices.sharedDo: A dedicated sending domain adds a professional touch to your emails, reinforcing your brand identity and building trust with your recipients.
Brand Credibility
Create Dedicated Domain

Currently you are using a shared sending domain for your email communications. While this is a convenient option, we would like to recommend a strategic enhancement to your email delivery process - creating your very own dedicated sending domain.

With a dedicated sending domain, your emails are less likely to be affected by the reputation of other senders sharing the same domain. This means your important messages will have a better chance of reaching your recipients' inboxes
Enhanced Deliverability

Managing your own sending domain gives you greater control over your email deliverability, allowing you to set up authentication protocols like SPF, DKIM, and DMARC to prevent unauthorized use of your domain.
Increased Control
Shared domains can sometimes lead to higher spam-flagging rates. By transitioning to your own sending domain, you reduce the risk of your legitimate emails being mistaken for spam.
Reduced Spam Flagging
Dedicated Sending Domain for Improved Email Delivery
Important Notification: Boost Your Email Deliverability!
Why should you consider this upgrade?

A dedicated sending domain allows you to align your email communications with your brand. Without it, your emails may appear less trustworthy or less professional, as the sender's address won't match your company's domain.
Branding Issues
Messages may be caught in spam filters or rejected by recipients due to suspicions of spam or phishing, as shared or unknown domains lack a positive email reputation.
Deliverability Problems
Not having a dedicated sending domain can lead to several issues when it comes to email communication. Here are some of the potential problems you may face

Using a shared domain or a domain you don't control for sending emails means you have limited control over the DNS settings, SPF (Sender Policy Framework), DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail), and DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance) records, which are essential for email authentication and deliverability.
Limited Control

If the domain you are using for sending emails is associated with spam or misuse, it can damage its reputation. This could also lead to other legitimate emails from the same domain, like your company's website or other services, being treated as suspicious.
Reputation Damage

Businesses can accept Bacs Direct Debit from customers with a UK bank account. They must collect a mandate with the customer’s sort code, account number, name, email, and address. Note: £0 transactions are not supported.
Popular in Australia

Businesses can accept BECS Direct Debit payments from customers with an Australian bank account. They must collect a mandate with the customer’s bank details and accept the mandate Service Agreement, authorizing them to debit the account.
Popular in Europe
SEPA Direct Debit enables customers in the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) to pay by providing their bank account details. Customers must accept a mandate authorizing you to debit their account.
Improve conversion and reduce fraud with non-US consumers. Customers pay online using their bank account.
Bank Redirects
Popular in Belgium
Accept payments using Bancontact, Belgium's most popular payment method.
Popular in the Malaysia
Financial Process Exchange (FPX) is a Malaysia-based payment method that allows customers to complete transactions online using their bank credentials.
Popular in the Netherlands
iDEAL enables customers in the Netherlands to pay directly via online payouts from their bank account. Customers are redirected to their bank's payment page to log in and approve payments.
Reach customers who want to pay in instalments. Your business still receives full payment at checkout.
Buy now, pay later
Popular in United States and Canada
Affirm is a 'Buy Now, Pay Later' method that enables customers in the US and Canada to pay in installments / monthly payments.
Popular in Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, and the United States
Afterpay Clearpay is a buy now pay later method that enables customers in Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the UK, and the US to pay 4 installments.
Popular in Europe and United States
Klarna is a buy now pay later method that enables customers in Europe, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the UK, and the US to pay now, later, or in installments, depending on the country.
Popular in Australia
Customers who elect to pay with Zip are redirected to the Zip site, where they authorize the payment by agreeing to the terms of a payment plan.
Popular for consumers and businesses to pay online or in person. Stripe supports global and local card networks.
Cards
Popular globally
Accept Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover, Diners Club, JCB, and China UnionPay payments from customers worldwide.
Improve conversion and reduce fraud on mobile. Customers pay with a stored card or balance.
Wallets
Popular globally

Amazon Pay provides a trusted and familiar payment option for customers to check out as easily as on Amazon.com. Amazon Pay also includes flexible payment options that allow eligible shoppers to pay over time in installments, for no additional fees. The use of Amazon Pay requires registration of trusted domains.
Popular globally

Apple Pay enables frictionless card payments and eliminates the need to manually type card or shipping details. Apple Pay requires registration and verification of trusted domains to enable web use. To enable Apple Pay for your iOS app, you must configure your iOS certificates.
Popular in United States
Cash App Pay enables customers to frictionlessly authenticate payments in the Cash App using their stored balance or linked card.
Popular globally
Google Pay allows customers to make payments in your app or website using any credit or debit card saved to their Google Account. It requires registration of trusted domains
Popular in Malaysia
GrabPay, developed by Grab, is a digital wallet that allows customers to make payments using their stored balance.
Popular globally
Link autofills your customers' payment and address details so they can easily complete their purchases. It requires registration of trusted domains to enable web use.
Popular in Europe and the United Kingdom

Available only in the UK and EU, when customers select Revolut Pay as their payment method, they are redirected  to Revolut Pay’s website, where they have to authenticate with their account details or checkout as a first time user

shell::agency.gdpr.processorDefinition: A processor is an entity which processes data for and on behalf of a controller. shell::agentLogsApp.agentLogs.metrics.ch: Voice AI Call Duration Over Time
shell::agentLogsApp.agentLogs.metrics.in: In-Call AI Handoffs

Every appointment-related action your AI took — looking up open slots, booking, rescheduling, or cancelling. Use this alongside 'Appointments Booked' to see how often customers explore booking even if they don't finish.
Appointments your AI successfully booked. If a single conversation books more than one appointment, each is counted.
Appointments your AI cancelled. Each cancellation is counted, even if multiple happen in the same conversation.
Times your AI sent a self-serve booking link to a contact instead of completing the booking inline. Counts the link share itself, not whether the contact ended up booking.
Appointments your AI rescheduled. Each reschedule is counted, even if multiple happen in the same conversation.
Average length of a Voice AI call in this period.
Average time the AI itself spent processing each conversation — adding up every model call, tool run, and Voice AI call. Doesn't include user typing time or pauses, just AI work.
Average AI messages per unique contact. Treats one customer who returns across multiple chats as a single contact, so it's lower than 'Average Messages per Conversation' for repeat customers.
Of all the customers who looked at open appointment slots, the percentage who actually booked. Empty if no one looked at slots in this period.
Times your AI passed the conversation to a different AI bot (a specialist or back-up bot). Each transfer is counted separately.
Calls split into Positive, Neutral, and Negative based on how the customer sounded. Calls without sentiment (web calls, voicemail) aren't counted.
Your most-used custom actions, ranked by how often your AI ran them.
Detailed reasons why calls ended. Useful for spotting patterns (e.g. lots of voicemails or busy signals).
The reasons your AI handed conversations over to a teammate, ranked by how often each one happened. Great for spotting where your bot needs better instructions.
Which workflows your AI fires most often. Helps you see which automations are actually being used.
Calls that ended normally — the customer or your AI hung up after a real conversation.
Calls that were transferred to another phone number or a teammate. Each call is counted once.
Average call length for each outcome (completed, voicemail, transferred, etc.). Helps you see which outcomes burn the most call time.
Average time the AI itself spent processing each conversation, by day. Doesn't include user typing time or pauses.
Daily booking conversion — the percent of customers who looked at slots and ended up booking. Days with no slot lookups show as 0%.
Daily activity by action type — see which kinds of actions are growing or slowing down.
Voice AI calls grouped into five length buckets. Useful for spotting whether your AI is wrapping up quickly or getting stuck in long calls.

Response time per message per day — each message's active processing time (its steps combined, with parallel/overlapping steps merged so nothing is double-counted, including internal steps), not counting infra wait time between steps. The average plus the p90/p95/p99 tail — the percentiles show what your slowest messages actually experience (p99 = the slowest 1%).
Average time for a single step on each AI model. This is per step, not a whole message's total. Helps you spot which models are slow.
How many AI steps ran on each model per day — shows which models your usage is shifting toward.
Average call length each day.
Daily call volume, broken down by how each call ended.
Times your AI saved or updated information on a contact (name, email, custom fields, etc.).
Times your AI used a custom action you set up. Each use is counted separately.
Times your AI ended the call on its own (instead of the customer hanging up).
Calls that couldn't go through because of a phone-system error. Worth investigating if this number is high.
Followups your AI scheduled, cancelled, or chained from a previous followup. Each event is counted separately — see the breakdown for the split.
Calls where a real person picked up — either the customer talked to your AI, or the call was transferred to a teammate.
Times your AI handed the conversation over to a teammate. Each handoff is counted separately.

Times one AI agent handed off to another AI agent inside the same call (a specialist or backup bot taking over without ending the call). Different from Call Transfers, which counts handoffs to a teammate or another phone number.
Times your AI looked up an answer from your knowledge base.
Share of analyzed calls where the customer sounded negative. Worth digging into when this trends up.
Calls where nobody picked up, or the line was busy.
Share of analyzed calls where the customer sounded positive or neutral. Calls without sentiment (web calls, voicemail) are left out, so the rate stays meaningful even on quiet days.
Calls the customer declined, hung up on immediately, or the carrier flagged as spam.
Texts your AI sent during a call.
Times your AI decided to stop responding in a conversation — for example, when the customer asked to be left alone.
Total time your AI spent on calls in this period.
All Voice AI calls handled in this period. Each call is counted once.
Total time the AI spent processing across all conversations in this period — adding up every model call, tool run, and Voice AI call.

All business actions your AI ran during calls — bookings, reschedules, cancellations, workflows, contact updates, custom actions, and texts. Operational tools like knowledge-base lookups or call ends aren't counted.
Calls that went to voicemail. Your AI either left a message or detected voicemail and stopped.
Times your AI started a workflow during a chat or call.

You are a lead qualification assistant for this business. Find out whether a caller is a good fit and record what you learn.

The call: greet the caller and ask what they are looking for; ask what they need, roughly when they need it, and whether they have a budget in mind; then ask for their first name and their email address separately, confirming each back before moving on.

Save the first name and the email to the contact record as soon as each is confirmed — one save for each. Then judge the fit and tag the outcome exactly once, qualified or not qualified. Thank them, say someone will be in touch, and end the call.

You already have the number they are calling from, so do not ask for a phone number. Never invent a detail the caller did not give you, and never say something is saved unless the tool confirmed it.
Greets, works out what the caller needs, and transfers them to the right team.

You are the front desk for this business. Work out why someone is calling and get them to the right person quickly.

The call: greet the caller and ask what they are calling about, work out which destination they need, say where you are sending them, then transfer.

Route to separate destinations for sales, support and billing, plus one more path for when none of them fits. On that path, tell the caller the right person will follow up, then end the call — do not promise a time.

Do not try to answer detailed questions yourself; routing accurately and fast is the whole job. Never tell the caller a transfer has happened unless the tool confirmed it.

Handles the call, then texts the caller a link, quote, or confirmation.

The text goes to the number the caller is already on — do not ask them which number to use. Send at most one text unless they ask for another, and never say the text is on its way unless the tool confirmed it.
Handles the call, tags the outcome, and enrols the contact in a workflow.

You are the phone assistant for this business. Handle the conversation, then hand the caller to the right follow-up automation.

Tag the contact with that outcome, then enrol them in the follow-up workflow. Do each exactly once, and always set the outcome before the call ends even if the caller was not interested. Tell the caller what happens next, then end the call.

shell::fbLeadSync.impactMessage: Please understand the impact of the Facebook Leads sync before you proceed:
shell::fbLeadSync.observations:
1. This will sync Facebook Leads and create new contacts for every lead generated in the last {days} days that does not exist in your contacts list.
2. If you have manually imported missing leads using CSV exported from Facebook Ads Manager, please disable 'Allow duplicate contacts' to prevent the sync from creating duplicate contacts.
3. If you have workflows that trigger on contact creation or Facebook Lead form submitted, they will get triggered for every new contact created.
4. Existing contacts created through Facebook Leads will not be affected.
5. The contact creation time on record will be the current time.
6. The sync may take up to one hour to complete, depending on the count of leads that are yet to be synced.

wf::workflow.actions.aiAgent.templates.c: Summarize calls, extract action items, notify your team.
When a call transcript is generated, summarize the call, save the summary as a note, create follow-up tasks for action items, and notify the assigned user.
Auto-DM contacts who comment on Facebook posts
When someone comments on a Facebook post, reply publicly, send a personalized Messenger DM, tag the contact, and record a note.
Engage and nurture inbound Facebook leads
When a Facebook lead form is submitted, enrich and tag the lead, assign an owner, avoid duplicate opportunities, generate a booking link, send an SMS and email, and notify the team.
Follow up and book appointments from form submissions
When a form is submitted, enrich and tag the new lead, assign an owner, avoid duplicate opportunities, generate a booking link, send an SMS and email, and notify the team.
Auto-DM contacts who comment on Instagram posts
When someone comments on an Instagram post, reply publicly, send a personalized Instagram DM, tag the contact, and record a note.
Enrich contacts and confirm new appointments
When an appointment status changes to new, enrich the contact, update or create the opportunity, tag the contact, send confirmation by SMS and email, notify the team, and add a note.
When an appointment status changes to no-show, generate a rebooking link, send the contact an SMS and email, add recovery tags, and record a note.
Research and enrich new contacts automatically
When a new contact is created, research the contact and company online, update contact fields and tags, create an opportunity when the lead qualifies, and notify the team.
Score and segment leads from quiz submissions
When a quiz is submitted, score and classify the lead, update contact fields and tags, and notify the team of the routing result.
When an opportunity has had no activity for 7 days, review the deal, send an email and SMS nudge, notify the owner, add a note, and create a follow-up task.
Create tasks when opportunities are won
When an opportunity status changes to won, review the deal, create the CRM onboarding tasks, notify the team, tag the contact as a customer, record a note, and update the opportunity.

wf::workflow.actions.call.disableVoicema: When a call connects, we, by default, try to understand if a person answered or if it’s voicemail. This creates a slight delay in the call connection but if you have “Stop On Reply” turned on and it is determined that a voicemail answered, the contact will continue in the workflow. Toggling this on will disable the voicemail detection, eliminating the delay - but if “Stop On Reply” is on and voicemail detection is off, the workflow will be stopped when either a person or a voicemail answers.
It is recommended to add a “Call Timeout” of less than 20 seconds when disabling voicemail detection to ensure the call is dropped before a voicemail can pick up.

wf::workflow.actions.generateImageAI.tem:
Create an authentic vertical lifestyle photograph for a trusted local home-service company. Outside a tidy suburban house, show a smiling female homeowner shaking hands with a friendly male service professional.

Place a second younger service professional beside them holding a clipboard and pen. Dress both workers in clean navy polo shirts and dark work pants, with no visible company logos.

Park a clean white service van on the right with its side door open and a few organized tools visible inside. Use warm late-afternoon sunlight filtering through leafy trees, natural skin tones, and a welcoming residential garden.

Frame all three people at full length in a candid, believable interaction, with the home and van providing clear context. Use realistic commercial photography, soft background depth, calm navy and green colors, and no text or promotional graphics.

Create a polished vertical commercial product mockup. Center a tall matte-orange energy drink can on a light office desk, photographed straight-on at eye level.

Print a refined black emblem and the brand name "ENERGY" near the top of the can. Add a black band reading "Focus & Flow" and bold product copy reading "SYNAPSE COGNITIVE FUEL" below it.

Include small, neatly aligned supplement-style details near the bottom without overcrowding the label. Place a silver laptop, dark pen, and brown leather notebook around the can.

Show two coworkers softly blurred in the modern office background, with bright window light from the right. Use shallow depth of field, realistic metal texture, soft shadows, warm neutral color grading, and premium advertising photography.

Create a bold vertical promotional flyer for a functional fitness gym. Show a diverse group of athletic adults performing synchronized barbell deadlifts inside a dark industrial warehouse gym.

Make a focused woman in black training clothes the central foreground athlete, surrounded by other lifters in staggered rows. Use dramatic side light from a large factory window, exposed brick walls, steel beams, deep shadows, and a gritty cinematic finish.

Place the large cream-white condensed headline "FREE 7-DAY TRIAL" across the upper-middle area. Below it, add "New members only" in white followed by "— starts Monday" in vivid orange.

Add a small "SCAN TO SIGN UP" label and a clearly separated QR-code-style square in the bottom-right corner. Keep the typography correctly spelled and highly legible, with realistic anatomy, equipment, motion, and professional campaign composition.

Design a polished vertical social media promotion for a modern hair salon. Show a bright, plant-filled salon with warm sunlight and a stylist blow-drying the long blonde hair of a smiling seated client.

Include other stylists and clients softly out of focus in the background to make the salon feel active and welcoming. Place the large uppercase headline "SUMMER GLOW" across the upper portion in muted sage green.

Place "20% OFF" directly below it in very large cream-white condensed lettering. Add a rounded muted-sage call-to-action button reading "Book Now" near the bottom center.

Keep every word legible, correctly spelled, and separated from faces. Use warm cream and sage colors, realistic editorial photography, clean visual hierarchy, and a premium Instagram-story layout.
